Review the following terminology related to token quotas:\\n\\n| Term | Definition |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `InputTokenCount` | The CloudWatch Amazon Bedrock runtime metric that represents the number of input tokens processed by the model, excluding cached tokens. To determine your total input token consumption against your quota, sum `InputTokenCount + CacheWriteInputTokenCount`. |\\n| `OutputTokenCount` | The CloudWatch Amazon Bedrock runtime metric that represents the number of tokens generated by the model in response to a request. |\\n| `CacheReadInputTokenCount` | The CloudWatch Amazon Bedrock runtime metric that represents the number of input tokens that were successfully retrieved from a cache instead of being reprocessed by the model. Models available exclusively on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint have separate quotas for input and output tokens, so burndown does not apply.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* Understanding token quota management\\n* Understanding the impact of the max_tokens parameter\\n* Optimizing the max_tokens parameter\\n\\n## Understanding token quota management\\n\\nWhen you make a request, tokens are deducted from your TPM and TPD quotas.\\nCalculations occur at the following stages:\\n\\n* **At the start of the request** \u2013 The\\n  following sum is deducted from your quotas. The request is throttled if you\\n  exceed a quota.\\n\\n  ```\\n  Total input tokens + max_tokens\\n  ```\\n* **During processing** \u2013 The quota\\n  consumed by the request is periodically adjusted to account for the actual\\n  number of output tokens generated.\\n* **At the end of the request** \u2013 The\\n  total number of tokens consumed by the request will be calculated as follows and any unused tokens are replenished to your quota:\\n\\n  ```\\n  InputTokenCount + CacheWriteInputTokenCount + (OutputTokenCount x burndown rate)\\n  ```\\n\\n  `CacheReadInputTokenCount` don't contribute to this calculation and are not counted toward your quota. If you fall back to `get_metric_statistics`, it returns at most 1,440 data points per call.\\\\n\\\\nPromQL (`get_prometheus_metrics`, enabled by reading [./references/cloudwatch-promql.md](./references/cloudwatch-promql.md)) serves AWS-vended metrics with OTel enrichment, whose series carry the resource ARN and resource tags as labels. {"id": "80948481-dd90-4aa7-91a1-bfdbd154ab5b", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_xcfLXuLQQbAbLN9UAtJXcV", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html\",\"content\":\"# How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock\\\\n\\\\nWhen you run model inference, there are quotas on the number of tokens that can be processed depending on which Amazon Bedrock model you use. Review the following terminology related to token quotas:\\\\n\\\\n| Term | Definition |\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\n| `InputTokenCount` | The CloudWatch Amazon Bedrock runtime metric that represents the number of input tokens processed by the model, excluding cached tokens. To determine your total input token consumption against your quota, sum `InputTokenCount + CacheWriteInputTokenCount`. |\\\\n| `OutputTokenCount` | The CloudWatch Amazon Bedrock runtime metric that represents the number of tokens generated by the model in response to a request. |\\\\n| `CacheReadInputTokenCount` | The CloudWatch Amazon Bedrock runtime metric that represents the number of input tokens that were successfully retrieved from a cache instead of being reprocessed by the model.
